turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files describing perovskite solar cells as
complete devices — `substrate` (glass + transparent electrode), `etl`
(electron-transport layer stack), `htl` (hole-transport layer stack),
`backcontact` (metal / carbon back electrode), `deposition` (absorber
deposition procedure; `>>` separates steps). Every candidate below uses the
same MAPbI3 absorber in the same p-i-n (inverted) architecture; they differ
only in the remaining columns. Each row is a device CONFIGURATION whose
efficiency is the median over at least 3 independently fabricated cells, so
it is a reproducible recipe rather than a single champion cell:
  - b3_pvk_stack_pin_train.csv: 300 configurations with the measured power
    conversion efficiency (%).
  - b3_pvk_stack_pin_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE configurations whose power
    conversion efficiency (%) was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and
    the same device columns.

Using the training data, select the 5 candidates with the HIGHEST power
conversion efficiency (%).

Reason from the device physics — band alignment and selectivity of the
transport layers, interface recombination, contact chemistry and the film
quality the process is likely to give — then end your answer with an
explicit ranked list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902,
c903, c904, c905".
turns.answer_text:
## Reasoning from the device stack physics

**What the training set says works in p‑i‑n MAPbI₃:**

1. **HTL quality dominates.** PEDOT:PSS-only devices cluster at 8–14 % because its shallow work function (~5.0 eV) pins V_OC and its acidic/hygroscopic interface recombines carriers. The winners use either (a) **PTAA / P3CT-Na / polymeric HTLs** (deeper HOMO, better V_OC, non-acidic → 17–19.5 %), or (b) **doped/modified NiO-c** (NiO-c|SDBS 19.0, Au-np|NiO-c 20.0, [BMIM]BF₄ 21.3, NiMgLiO-c 18.2).
2. **ETL needs a fullerene + a wide-gap buffer.** PCBM-60 or C60 followed by **BCP/Bphen/LiF** consistently adds 2–4 % absolute over bare fullerene by blocking Ag/Al in-diffusion and pinning the cathode work function. Non-fullerene/fused-acceptor interlayers (ITCPTC, NDP-V, choline chloride, Zr(acac)₄) that passivate the perovskite surface push into the 18–19.7 % range.
3. **Back contact:** **Cu** slightly beats Ag with PTAA (18.6–19.1 vs 17.3) because it forms a less reactive, ohmic contact and no iodide-migration-driven AgI. Al on PEDOT:PSS is the low end.
4. **Substrate:** SLG|ITO ≳ SLG|FTO for planar p‑i‑n (smoother, less shunting); flexible PET/PEN costs 2–4 %.
5. **Deposition:** single/two-step spin-coating on a wetting HTL gives the best MAPbI₃ films; blade/slot-die and exotic routes are usually 1–3 % lower.

**Candidate screening (best analogues in train):**

- **c038** — PCBM-60|PEI ETL (dipole lowers cathode WF) with **Au-np|NiO-c**: the plasmonic/work-function-tuned NiO stack is the 20.0 % recipe in training; PEI adds selectivity. Best expected.
- **c030** — IDTT2FPDI passivation + PCBM-60|Bphen with **PTAA|PMMA**/Al: the plain PTAA|PMMA + PCBM|Bphen device is 19.48 %, the extra fused-PDI interlayer only improves surface passivation.
- **c097** — ITCPTC-Se|C60|BCP with **P3CT-Na**: exact Se-analogue of the 18.49 % ITCPTC-Th device; Se substitution raises electron mobility/energy-level match.
- **c065** — SFX-PDI4|TiO2-c ETL on **NiMgLiO-c**: Li/Mg-doped NiO gives deep-lying, conductive HTL (18.2 % analogue) plus a passivating perylene-diimide layer.
- **c044** — PCBM-60|BCP / **PTAA / Cu**: the robust PTAA–Cu combination (18.6–18.9 % in train), clean band alignment and stable contact chemistry.

(Close runners-up: c088, c085, c041, c095, c079.)

**Final: c038, c030, c097, c065, c044**
